summary: Groundwork for child chats on other machines (design 2026-10-29): the VM backend lifecycle and token. This part is not gated by a flag. the remote bootstrap starts the headless backend and the managed code-server detached (setsid nohup, output in ~/.switchboard-server/server.log), so a tunnel drop, a desktop sleep or a quit no longer ends the sessions on the VM. Each connect reuses a live backend when its pid is still ours, it was started from the installed version (server.version equals version) and its HTTP listener answers within 3 s; otherwise it reaps the backend and code-server as before and starts fresh ones. The ssh session waits on the backend pid, so the tunnel ends when the server dies. The backend now always runs with a token: the bootstrap keeps it 0600 in ~/.switchboard-server/token and prints it once on the ssh channel; the desktop reads it from the tunnel output (never logged), keeps it in memory, sends it in the health probe and gives it to the renderer through a desktop-only IPC call (not the backend host, which also serves phones). The renderer sends it in an auth frame; WsHost accepts the server token in an auth frame with the same scopes as the URL token. On reuse, a code-server that does not answer on its port is reaped and started again. The bootstrap sets 0600 on an existing token file and exits when it cannot create a token. Scope hub and the hub-remote skeleton (PR 2), behind the staged flag hub_remote_children (HUB_REMOTE_CHILDREN_ENABLED in src/shared/hub.ts, false; SB_HUB_REMOTE_CHILDREN=1 or the backend setting labs.hub_remote_children turns it on, and only while hub_children is on). A new DeviceScope hub opens the hub-remote:* channels and events and nothing else; every other channel now needs chat, which every phone, device session, server token and the IAP TCP host already holds (a stored device row without chat gets it, and hub is dropped from any device credential). Only the server token grants hub: its auth frame may carry scopes, and the backend grants the asked scopes the token holds (hub when it holds admin) or refuses the auth. The capability hub_remote_child_v1 is advertised. hub-remote:describe answers on the desktop and the headless server, with the flag off too: flag state, OS, architecture, backend version, agents that run there with their enabled accounts and catalog models, up to 200 projects with branch and fetch remote URLs (git with a 5 s timeout, one bad repository does not fail the answer), free disk under ~/projects or home, open children and run slots per account. It holds no host name, cloud project, zone or user name. The events hub-remote:outbox and hub-remote:children-changed are declared without an emitter. The desktop hub client and list_machines (PR 3), behind hub_remote_children: RemoteHubClients in the desktop main process opens one WebSocket client per connected machine from the ConnectionManager status (tunnel URL and backend token, ?auth=frame, auth frame scopes hub), accepts only an authed of exactly hub and a ready with hub_remote_child_v1 (otherwise it closes and the machine reads 'update the backend on <name>'), closes on disconnect, delete and quit, refuses a call to a machine that is not connected at once and times a call out after 20 s, with a hub.remote-call perf line per call. It reads hub-remote:describe on every connect and at most every 60 s on demand, keeps an offline machine's last answer with its age and caches no failure. A parent chat that is not an open child, on the desktop's own backend (not SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE), gets the read-only tool list_machines and one more instruction line while the flag is on: this desktop first, then each saved machine with id, the user's name for it, transport, status, OS and architecture, agents with accounts and models, checkouts whose git remote matches the chat project's (https, ssh and scp forms compare as one key), free disk, open children, free run slots, and a line when the flag is off there or the backend needs an update. It never writes a host name, ssh alias, cloud project, zone or user name. With the flag off no client opens and the tool and line are absent. machine on start_children tasks, the batch card and propose checks (PR 4), behind hub_remote_children: a task may name a machine id from list_machines (type and length checked; local or absent is this machine), documented in the tool schema only where list_machines is offered. With the flag off, or from a parent on a VM, such a task is refused. Propose checks each remote task against the hub client's cached description (known, connected, no client problem, a fresh description, flagOn there, a login and the named account and model, a worktree location, a parent project with a git remote), uses a checkout there whose remote matches or plans a clone into ~/projects/<repo>, resolves the base to a commit a remote branch holds (the parent's upstream first; Switchboard does not push) and checks that machine's free disk against its own floor; the first problem refuses the batch, naming the task. The stored plan carries machine, remoteProjectPath, clonePlanned and fetch; a plan stored before reads as local. A batch with any remote child always opens the card, in every mode, with the machine per row, the clone note and one disk line per machine in the card and its plain text. Approval re-reads the machines; a machine that is gone, offline or lost the account fails only its own children. Local children in the batch start as before. The start path on the child machine (PR 5), behind hub_remote_children: a new channel hub-remote:start-child (scope hub or admin) and capability hub_remote_start_v1; a machine without it reads 'update the backend on <name>' at propose and approval. On approval the desktop sends each remote child to its machine through the hub client, at most 2 at once per machine, with its desktop install id (setting hub.installId, minted once), parent and child ids, title, brief, agent, account, model, granted mode, base commit, the branch to fetch, the remote URL without credentials and the dependency setting (both recorded in the plan when it is made, the URL read in the parent's own checkout; a plan stored before reads the URL in the project folder and sends the live setting), the task's own branch (same rule as a local task), the checkout path and whether to clone. The card shows the dependency setting on remote rows as on local ones. The child machine refuses with the flag off there, refuses a parent id or child id that names a chat or a hub parent there, answers a child it already has with its state and starts nothing, refuses over hub.remoteChildrenPerMachine (default 4, clamped 1 to 12) and an unknown account, lowers the mode to hub.remoteMaxMode (default auto) and answers the mode used, records a parent stub (hub_parents.remote_hub), clones the remote into the planned folder with its own git when one was planned (same URL checks and cleanup as project clone), refuses a missing folder without a planned clone and a folder with no configured remote of that URL, fetches the branch from that configured remote into a scratch ref and checks the base commit is in it, checks its own disk floor, and runs the same worktree, dependency, run slot, session and brief steps as a local child, seeding the branch from the task's branch or else its title. It answers once the child is open or failed, or 'starting' after 12 s. The desktop row records the machine (hub_children.machine_id) and the mode used; a refusal or an older backend fails only that child with a failed wake that names the machine, and one child's throw fails that child only. A timeout or a closed client leaves the row starting: the same request, rebuilt from the stored plan, is sent again every 15 s up to 2 minutes after such a call or a starting answer, on each connect of that machine and at launch, and its answer applies only while the row is still starting; a machine the user removes fails its starting children. A remote child that leaves starting lets local children waiting for a run slot go. On the desktop, recovery, the idle reaper, the resource sampler and lineage edges skip a remote child; settle and an archive through it refuse while one is open, naming it ('Settling children on other machines comes in a later version: <titles>.'), after settling the local ones; list_children shows its machine and agent from the plan, and read_child on it says 'Reading a child on another machine comes in a later version.'; runningPerParent and the open-children cap still count it, keyed so no local account matches; Stop on it says 'Stop on another machine comes in a later version.'. On the child machine the wake scheduler never sends a turn to a parent stub. The outbox, pull and ack (PR 6), behind hub_remote_children: on the child machine every wake for a parent stub (report, failed, blocked, stopped, limited, resumed, restart) is a hub_outbox row (additive table: id, child, parent stub, kind wake or message, payload, created, acked) with the summary, the tool call and time of the pointer without the transcript path, and the child's phase, never a local wake; older stub wakes move there once on migration. A child's send_agent_message to its stub parent (listed to the child as its parent on another machine) is a message row (16 KiB cap, at most 60 unacked per child, its delivery kept); every other target keeps today's rules. Each insert emits hub-remote:outbox to hub and admin sessions only. New channels hub-remote:outbox-pull (items of that desktop's stubs, unacked, in order, after a cursor, 100 per page by default and 500 at most) and hub-remote:outbox-ack (that desktop's items only, idempotent, 500 at most) for hub and admin, answered with the flag off too, and the capability hub_remote_outbox_v1; acked rows are deleted after 7 days. The desktop pulls on that event, on each connect, at launch and after its hub client reconnects or misses events, one pull at a time per machine, page by page, only from a machine that advertises the capability, and acks each item only after its import committed; hub_remote_imports (additive) records each import by machine and item id so a re-pull imports nothing twice. An item counts only for a desktop child row of that machine and that parent: an item for another machine's child, a local child or an unknown child is recorded as dropped. A wake becomes a desktop wake (hub_wakes.machine_id, additive) through the same scheduler, so one batched update turn follows; a failed or stopped wake written at a failed start there ends the row failed_start. A message is delivered to the parent along the lineage edge, which now includes children on other machines and is charged first (60 messages); a refusal is recorded and not retried, and a parent that is not running is tried again every 60 s up to 5 times. A hub.outbox-pull perf line per pull. PR 7, view, read, deliver, interrupt, stop and move (capability hub_remote_control_v1, flag hub_remote_children): the child machine answers hub-remote:view, read-child, deliver, interrupt, stop (with an optional settle), move and stop-all only for a child of that desktop's parent stub, and emits hub-remote:children-changed with the stub ids that changed. The desktop routes each action on a remote child through its machine: list_children and the strip merge a cached view per machine (read on that event, on connect and when older than 15 s; a machine that is not connected shows its last view with its age and not connected), read_child and interrupt_child call the machine, a parent's message or Nudge charges the lineage edge here first and is then delivered there as queue or steer, move_child goes to an account on the child's own machine only, a settle stops the child there and applies that machine's settle rules against the parent's HEAD, and an archive sends stop-all. A Stop, settle or stop-all for a machine that is not connected is kept in hub_remote_pending (additive table) and sent on its next connect before anything else; the child shows Stopping on the machine until it is answered. A machine without the capability keeps the earlier later-version texts. Opening a remote child's transcript from the desktop is a follow-up. PR 8, desktop UI (flag hub_remote_children; with it off no view carries a remote field and nothing renders differently): a child on another machine gets a machine badge (its name, mono and muted) in the children strip and on a nested sidebar row (a remote child has no conversation on the desktop, so in practice the strip); its state text adds the machine for Waiting for a slot, Needs approval and Reconnecting, and a machine that is not connected shows the dot as Unknown with '<machine> offline, last seen <age>', the age from the cached view or else the machine's last synced tree (machine_snapshots.synced_at), so it survives a restart; Stop stays offered for such a child and is queued as before. The batch card shows a remote row's machine as a badge with its transport tag (IAP or SSH) after the agent, model and account, then the mode. The Hub chip reads 'Hub · N children on M machines' when M > 1. The hub view served to phones already carries remote.machineId and remote.machine with connected, reconnecting, ageMs and stopping; childStateLabel and childStateWord (shared) give the state text, and tests/fixtures/hub-cases.json gains childStateText and childrenCount cases for the phone ports. Perf: hub.remote-reconnect (machine, down ms, open children there, outbox items pulled), and machineId on hub.child-turn and hub.wake. PR 10, reconnect on launch and failure polish (flag hub_remote_children; with it off nothing changes and the Settings switch is hidden): at launch the desktop connects each saved, offline machine that holds open (starting or open) children of its hubs (hub_children.machine_id) through the normal connect path, so the pending-stop flush, the start reconcile and the outbox pull run as on any connect. The backend setting hub.reconnectOnLaunch (default on) turns it off, from a switch 'Reconnect machines with running children on launch' under Settings > Devices & machines > Machines, shown only while the flag is on (read through machines:hub-remote-enabled). ssh runs with BatchMode, so a connect that needs a login, a 2FA or a host key prompt fails, retries only on the connection's existing backoff and leaves the machine offline, which the strip shows as before. Perf: one hub.remote-launch-reconnect line (machines tried, connected, ms); hub.remote-reconnect fires only for a machine that came back within a run. On a child machine whose backend starts again, recoverInterrupted still marks starting children failed_start with a failed wake, and now gives each open child of a parent stub one restart wake (none when its last wake is already restart), which goes to the outbox; local children get none. On a machine reached over SSH, hub-remote:describe lists only Claude Code and Codex accounts that sign in there (the remote start's login check on the default folder passes, then a key in the account's env or a login in its folder; an account whose folder only an encrypted env names is not listed), so an agent with no login is not listed and propose refuses with '<agent> has no login on <machine>. Log in there first (claude, codex login, opencode auth login).'. On a child machine, a child from another machine's hub that fails to start (or is stopped before its first turn) has its session stopped and its worktree removed through the same removal a settle uses, which deletes the branch the creation made and never a pre-existing one; a local child keeps its worktree. A Claude login the CLI refused (authentication_failed on a session in that config folder, with no key in the env) counts as signed out in the remote login check, and so in hub-remote:describe and list_machines, until its .credentials.json changes (a new sign-in or a token refresh), because the file stays on disk after a login expires. Phones (PR 9): the backend advertises hub_remote_children_v1 in the ready frame only while hub_remote_children is on. With it, the Hub row on Expo and Android shows a remote child's machine badge, its state text from childStateLabel (the machine for a slot, an approval, a reconnect or a Stop, offline with its age), its Stop to the child's own id (the desktop forwards or queues it), and its Open shows the child's newest report summary (No report yet. when none) and Read on the desktop. Without it the phones drop the view's remote field, so nothing renders differently.
